summary: Each claim append looks up its custom invalidations by claim ID instead of walking every document binding

replay.detail: Existing custom projection rows remain valid; no claim replay or cache rebuild is required.

schema.detail: The local custom_claim_invalidations view's document-binding branch writes its kind filter as +binding.kind, so SQLite looks binding claims up by the claim IDs each trigger names instead of walking every doc.bound claim through claims_kind_index. Store open replaces an installed older view once, as it already does for the custom triggers; an unchanged reopen keeps the schema cookie. No table, column, index, storage version or rules version changes.

rules.detail: The view returns the same rows; only its query plan changes. Signed claim authority, canonical ordering and custom projection results are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No public API, replication protocol or claim format changes. The view is local and never compared between members.

downtime.detail: The normal store-open schema transaction replaces the view.

recovery.detail: Earlier builds create the view only if it is missing, so a rollback keeps this definition, which returns the same rows; custom projections remain derived caches recoverable from the signed claim log.
